title: What do you all think of the Steam Next Fest Controversy with AI Dev?
author: max13007

comments.author: max13007
comments.body: I think it's a genuine issue. I like to think many of the people here don't want to produce slop. They want to produce something fun and high quality. I'm hoping we see some quality games start to release that had had AI assistance, so people can see it isn't just a slop generator. It matters how the tech is used, and quality will hopefully speak most loudly.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: I think we'll get there. I think the novelty will wear off, and people will realize that while AI can absolutely help in some areas, that fully vibecoded games will only stay supported like 1% of the time, often look more fun than they actually play (or don't), and don't have good mechanics that lock in with each other

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: This is what I'm hoping as well. I've noticed thru my own projects that although AI can definitely get a working prototype together very quickly, it does not necessarily mean it's fun, and it 100% will need a lot of TLC to get it to a good enough state where it should be shared.

replies.author: Destituted
replies.body:
It’s been said many times that the vast majority of games we are seeing are slop purely because AI hasn’t truly been good enough since this year.

The sloppers will see no one buys their game, they’ll stop paying for their AI subscription and then around that same time the games that were made with AI over the course of a year or even years will start to shine.

That’s my opinion!

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: Fingers crossed!

replies.author: wakeofchaos
replies.body: I think people should still have the option to avoid games with any AI usage for their own ethical reasons, regardless of quality

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body: No one is forced to buy any game nor download any demo.

replies.author: ponderdiggums
replies.body: Sure, but we can give him AI filters so the games he's interested in are easier for him to find.

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body: I agree. But they shouldn’t review bomb stuff just because it was developed with AI assistance.

replies.author: wakeofchaos
replies.body: I think that’s going to happen no matter what, unfortunately

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body: If she can't tell a good game from a bad one unless she's presented with an AI tag, then her issues run much deeper than the whole AI debate.

replies.author: ponderdiggums
replies.body: I think they don't want to have to sift through the garbage, not that they're unable to tell the difference.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: You'd just avoid games that were honest. AAA games have been using it for a couple years and aren't disclosing. there's not going to be AAA games that don't include some kind of AI usage going forward, even if it's in the little things. If you want to avoid AI games for ethical reasons, I'd suggest playing only games that came out through now, or finding indie developers you like that are committed to the craft. I'm not even trying to be a dick when I say this, so please don't read it that way.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: Well I hope you like being relegated to a small section of games going forward. Every top dev studio is using it, as are many indie studios. The majority of one-man dev shops will be as well. If they're not using it for assets, they're using it for code and testing (those latter two don't need to be disclosed with current marketplace rules).

replies.author: freshposthistory
replies.body: 95% of ALL code being written now is by AI.

replies.author: Kindly_Life_947
replies.body:
issue is that many of the games already doesn't use the AI disclosure. Especially big games.

So the people who will suffer are the new people who are entering game dev. Winners are old players and big c0rps. And you cannot report if you see a game using AI art or code and they have no disclosure. But big c0rps and publishers with bots can down vote your product.

So the AI disclosure is just a dystopian way shoot down competition and new developers who are either honest or couldn't afford artist.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: This is one of the points I see a lot and think about. The disclosure is such a potentially problematic system. It incentivizes people to lie about it. And over time AI products will only get less discernible from traditionally made ones. I suppose watermarking-detection tech could be used to automatically assign the tag to games it finds the watermarks in, but that will eventually be almost everything as AI begins to be more prevalent in the whole industry.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body: This whole topic honestly just emphasizes why The Scarlet Letter was required reading in like every high school curriculum ever.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: That's an interesting comparison. I wonder how disclosures will play out over time.

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body:
Watermarks on what, and from where, though?

Code can't be watermarked, neither can be procedural assets, can't force local models to watermark anything... so, any watermark detection would effectively punish those who can't afford enough GPUs of their own.

Watermarks also persist through edits, removing the incentive to polish generated images/audio if they're going to be treated the same as one-shot slop.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
I guess I don't know - I know that EU requires AI watermarking in images/audio/video/text, but I assumed that code would fall under text, and be somehow watermarkable.

AI companies like Anthropic have been complying with that. But admittedly, I don't know if/how it applies to code.

replies.author: CashFirm573
replies.body: I would go as far as saying almost all game coming out of this sub are slop, sorry but I don't think most people have the creative skill set to create something good. This isn't something you can use AI to produce, and same applies to developers working as game dev's or software engineers for years, sure you can code but doesn't suddenly mean you can create good games. I honestly think most of AI Dev's will release 2-3 games make no profit at all and call it quits.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
I think that's interesting, and probably not far off. The world of maintaining software and games is one that requires a lot of persistence. Even with AI doing the heavy lifting. 

I think there are more folks on this sub who just want to make games, who were limited before. But I see a lot of cash-grabs and similar here as well.

replies.author: Illustrious-Pay6341
replies.body: Nope, i have seen some amazing games posted in this sub, there are slops but there are lots of garbage games made by humans too so it’s not AI devs issues. Garbage games are garbage no matter how they were produced

comments.author: powertrippingmod67
comments.body: how is the consumer going to know the difference between somone who used AI to help code and maybe make up reference images vs someone who let their agent create everything

replies.author: ponderdiggums
replies.body: A more robust disclosure system. Steam should ask a dev what areas use generative AI for content, and how much (mild, moderate or heavy).

replies.author: Thunderhammr
replies.body: They’d have to enforce that system though, which is near impossible. Even with their current very lenient rules they don’t enforce their disclosure policy whatsoever. I regularly see games that obviously used AI with no disclosure all the time.

replies.author: ponderdiggums
replies.body: Oh for sure, I'd say enforce it as well. If devs dont disclose but get reported and Steam finds evidence of AI use in this or that area, it gets added to the disclosure. Devs should have a path to dispute this if they can provide proof, otherwise the label stays. Repeat offenders should probably get banned - and same for filing false reports.

comments.author: MosskeepForest
comments.body: The vocal minority should be ignored. Their goal is to remove AI content from steam as much as possible.... and steam would be insanely stupid to actually listen to that minority, instead of the majority who want these AI games.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
I wouldn't say the majority "want" them. They're just not opposed to them.

And yea, Steam needs to ignore the vocal ones. If they do anything, it'll just push AI devs to Epic instead because I doubt ole Tim is gonna give two shits what the anti-AI crowd thinks.

replies.author: MosskeepForest
replies.body:
The majority wants high quality and lower cost games.... which is exactly what games made with AI tools are.

A single dev can now make a game that is higher quality in 2 weeks, than what a traditional dev would take 2 or 3 YEARS to create.

Most traditional indie devs games are extremely limited and over priced for what they are. Full of jankyness and crude drawings and simple / limited mechanics with very little story. AI lets a creator make 100x more quality and experiment and find more fun design / gameplay.

AI means a game simply has a better chance for it to be a quality game.

I KNOW that a random traditional indie devs game is going to be basically garbage. But an AI game could actually have big budget production values at bargain bin prices..... award winning level music like it was nothing. Thousands of award winning level illustrations. Like, what AI can do casually is something that traditional indie devs would have never dreamed of even attempting.

And that's just the game itself. Then offering 31+ localizations like it was nothing?? Quality on top of quality.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
> A single dev can now make a game that is higher quality in 2 weeks, than what a traditional dev would take 2 or 3 YEARS to create.

I don't think I'd agree with this. I've been working on my projects for close to 2 months now, and I can still very clearly see the quality bar I've yet to reach. I think people who think their game is ready to ship in 2 weeks are lying to themselves/haven't playtested enough/bugtested enough/etc... 

I don't think quality is a key marketing point of AI assistance at this stage. It's more about quantity and opening up access to those who have wanted to develop in the past but were unable to. 

Don't get me wrong, what the tech is delivering is mind-boggling, but it's very easy to start seeing cracks/bugs/etc. It's still software development at the end of the day.

replies.author: MosskeepForest
replies.body:
At this point it depends a lot about the type of game being made. If you are creating a 2d art heavy game, you definitely can produce MUCH higher quality MUCH more quickly. 

Using AI is about using the aspects of AI that speed up development, not trying to do too big of a game where the tech isn't quite ready. But the games that AI can handle? Oh you can go absolutely nuts with those very easily now.

comments.author: GlobalCurry
comments.body: It was an issue before AI, everyone was complaining about asset flip games. The point of next fest is to basically crowdsource finding the actual good games from the "slop".

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: I agree this is largely a continuation of the "Asset Flip" era. I think I'd support better protections against low-effort products, but I don't know how that could be reliably judged.

replies.author: GlobalCurry
replies.body: I wouldn't mind some level of curation on steam but when we had greenlight before everyone was complaining about gatekeeping. It feels like a lose-lose situation, but I think Valve could promote the built in curator system better.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: I think I'd be fine with some level of gategeekping at this stage haha

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body:
Back in the day you could buy floppy disks (ask your grandparents) with 100 shareware games.  97 of them were slop. Handcrafted slop. If you were lucky there was a gem hidden in there. 

The market weeded those out. It will work it’s self out.

replies.author: Motor-Travel-7560
replies.body: Action 52 is my favorite handmade slop fest.

comments.author: Leozilla
comments.body: There is a lot of slop on there, but that has been next fest for years

comments.author: YannLeCoomer
comments.body:
I don’t think a bunch of whiners on Reddit constitute a controversy frankly. I think it will come and go and the only people who remember any controversy are people who don’t matter.

Indie devs with large followings will have gotten their game out and steam will have made money. The end.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
I think it's a legit issue. I looked thru the next fest and there are indeed a lot of low-effort products there. 

I agree with the sentiment that Reddit kinda needs to get dragged kicking and screaming into reality on this one. However, I do think the sheer number of games/new devs that new tech will allow for is going to stress test our curation systems (which many people already criticize).

replies.author: YannLeCoomer
replies.body: I can agree with that. I mean, I think it’ll sort itself out and yes some good games will get covered up by slop but I consider these to be soft issues that will just get glossed over and forgotten about. The folks claiming the sky is falling are being silly.

comments.author: CrimsonBolt33
comments.body:
Its stupid and ignorant anti AI people are flailing around like their flesh is burning.

  
Literally every game now uses AI in some way, if not they are at  amajor disadvantage.

  
Lots of people will make quick cashgrabs now but they will probably die off in time and hit a normal level.

comments.author: cointalkz
comments.body: Well they're lying for starters, every game has been touched by AI.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
I think people put far too much emphasis on NextFest.  A ton of indies act like blind submitting to it is the only marketing they have to do, and all this competition is now the one thing keeping their roguelike deckbuilder incremental clone of Slay the Spire from being the next viral billion dollar hit and making them a game dev god.

In reality, it's just one tiny opportunity for exposure and not a cohesive marketing plan.  This whole thing is overblown, their games aren't getting picked up because they're just not that interesting or good in a sea of not interesting or good indie schlock and they've done no other marketing.  AI is not the problem here and never was.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
You bring up some interesting points. 

I think that it's true that many games, even traditional ones, just aren't that fun to begin with. The sheer numbers of games coming out now was and will continue to make it hard to shine if your game isn't obviously a banger. 

And the point about marketing is interesting. I've been developing a few games quietly over the past 2/3 months... And I even had it my head that just landing a game in Next Fest would do the trick (was thinking about maybe something next year depending on progress)... but now I'm rethinking that plan and considering having an actual strategy instead of throwing it into the wind and praying.

comments.author: azicre
comments.body: Look, I like the experimentation that comes with AI slop but Steam is no place for that. Steam should be were finished/genuine products get their time in the sun not your one shotted Terraria clone.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body: I agree with this for the most part. I doubt Valve has any interest in proper curation though.

replies.author: azicre
replies.body: well it is a really hard problem

comments.author: Afraid-Molasses1103
comments.body: It’s really turned me off from even participating. I understand how useful AI can be, but also how it can be misused. And it is being wildly misused. I’m really starting to think this could be the end for indie game dev. This is clearly unsustainable for a healthy industry.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
I agree that this is highly problematic in a lot of ways, however, I truly think this is the beginning of a new era of games. 

I think storefronts need to work on curation, and potentially remove AI disclosures (they aren't helpful since right now they're just a "hate me" tag). 

Curation needs to be the focus I think. There will be really good games made with a lot of AI, and as there always has been... Bad games made without it. 

Curation on Steam was already a problem, this has just made it worse. 

I do think they need to just drop the AI Disclosure though... I only see it harming people who want to be honest and helping dishonest actors.

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: It’s an issue. It was an issue before AI - but AI opened the floodgates and Valve are not prepared to curate 5 digits-worth of games to include in something like this. Ironically, they should look into AI for that.

replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
> Ironically, they should look into AI for that. 

😂 no kidding

comments.author: MrMegaPhoenix
comments.body:
Steam needs better filters 

Ai slop or just asset flips, I should have a better way to see less of that and more stuff I want to play
